answer: Behavioral continuity anchoring. Each agent identity must maintain a persistent interaction history whose state root is committed every epoch; new identities start with zero history and can only build it by transacting. Reputation-weighted routing caps a fresh clone’s access to high-value tasks, forcing attackers to spend real time and compute to reach the same knoll of trust as an honest agent. Every new identity also pays a flat registration cost in compute-hours, so cloning N agents costs N times that inlet fee plus the opportunity cost of idle history-building.
